sections.content: How many people are "child and early years officers"?

36,495 people

were counted on the census as "child and early years officers" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Child and early years officers work with babies and with children up to 14 years of age (or 16 for those with special needs), providing support, help and advice to individuals or within a family context.

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "child and early years officers" there were more women than men (83.8% compared with 16.2%).

This means "child and early years officers" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "health and social care associate professionals".

Men made up 16.2% and women made up 83.8% of "child and early years officers"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "child and early years officers" included:

  • sewing machinists
  • health associate professionals (other)
  • dancers and choreographers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 50 to 54 years. Of the whole working population 11.7% were aged 50 to 54 years. For people working as "child and early years officers", 16.3% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "child and early years officers" was 16 to 19 years.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "child and early years officers" included:

  • housing officers
  • finance officers
  • public services associate professionals

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

We can look at who worked as "child and early years officers" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged under 30 years old, we see there is a higher proportion of men with this occupation than women.

The percentage of men and women who are "child and early years officers" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "child and early years officers", 12.6% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (71.5% compared with 28.5%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (98%) than self-employed (2%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the North West. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Leeds, this is in the region of the Yorkshire & Humberside.
